records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Each public embed request performs an uncached, unindexed case-insensitive host lookup, adding a table scan and database round trip at traffic scale.
records.rationale: The mechanism is verifiable in the diff: embeddable_host.rb adds `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (record_for_host), called from EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? on every public embed request via embed_controller's ensure_embeddable, and the migration (20150818190757) creates the table with no index on host, let alone a functional index on lower(host). So each embed request does an unindexed case-insensitive scan. This is not a correctness defect (behavior is correct), but it is a specific, substantive performance/scalability concern grounded in cited diff code.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The category lookup returns no row for the default blank `embed_category`, so dereferencing `[0]['id']` aborts migration before the fallback can preserve any embedding configuration.
records.rationale: In the migration, `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` is dereferenced unconditionally. When `embed_category` is blank (the default, ''), the site_settings row either doesn't exist or doesn't match a category name, so the result set is empty and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError before the `if category_id == 0` fallback can run — aborting the migration and preventing the embeddable_hosts data migration and site_settings cleanup that follow.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The category lookup returns no row for the default blank `embed_category`, so dereferencing `[0]['id']` aborts migration before the fallback can preserve any embedding configuration.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — The migration dereferences the first embed-category override row before checking for its absence, so upgrades fail on sites that retain the default unset setting.
records.rationale: The migration runs `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i` with no nil/empty check. Discourse site settings with unset defaults have no DB row, so on sites that never overrode embed_category the query returns an empty result set and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, failing the migration. The code only guards `category_id == 0` afterward, which doesn't help when the array is empty.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Copying legacy URL/path host-list entries verbatim bypasses normalization, so entries such as `http://discourse.org` no longer match the new hostname-only lookup and existing embeds are rejected after deploy.
records.rationale: The migration copies legacy `embeddable_hosts` values verbatim via raw SQL INSERT, bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization (host.sub! of scheme/path). EmbeddableHost.record_for_host then matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against the bare URI hostname, so stored entries like 'http://discourse.org' (the old setting format explicitly allowed hostnames not beginning with http, but the tests in this diff show values like 'http://eviltrout.com' were valid) would never match after migration, breaking existing embeds.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Copying legacy URL/path host-list entries verbatim bypasses normalization, so entries such as `http://discourse.org` no longer match the new hostname-only lookup and existing embeds are rejected after deploy.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Unescaped legacy host values are interpolated into SQL, so a URL path containing an apostrophe breaks the upgrade and crafted stored values can alter the statement.
records.rationale: The migration directly interpolates legacy `embeddable_hosts` values into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. A stored host value containing an apostrophe breaks the SQL, and since these values come from admin-configured site settings, the unescaped interpolation is a genuine SQL-injection/escaping defect introduced by this diff.
records.stripped_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Unescaped legacy host values are interpolated into SQL, so a URL path containing an apostrophe breaks the upgrade and crafted stored values can alter the statement.
